It is also because characters who have been part of your life for several years are dead and gone. I don’t mean the ones who died in the course of the actual war, but the others. Most of them faced rather tragic and unenviable ends. Along that personal voyage, the Mahabharata changes you, or so my wife tells me. I am no longer the person I was when I started it, as an individual. That sounds cryptic, deliberately so. Anyone who reads the Mahabharata carefully is bound to change, discount the temporary and place a premium on the permanent. To all those who have been part of that journey, including the readers, thank you. The original ten volumes were published sequentially, as they were complet- ed, between 2010 and 2014.
